scope: Common request/resource/lifetime contracts for token-generation and scoring consumers through Model/Session/Backend, and the component libraries engines call from their sessions (text, sampling, state cache, model files, host memory). Execution strategies and backend-specific techniques are opt-in.
factory: Static Factory returns a Model through public crit interfaces.
text_frontend: Optional independent host TextFrontend supports concurrent tokenize/detokenize calls during generation. Private TextDecoder instances retain their frontend, validate IDs, and outlive Engine. Request text and stop strings require it: Core decodes accepted tokens with the frontend's decoder (created without prompt context) or crit/text.h offset_decoder seeded with the prompt tail, applies one trim rule on both paths (stop tokens, output budget, then the first completed stop string) before commit, and fails only that request on a decoder or text reservation failure. Legacy model callbacks remain idle-only; their defaults throw.
resources: Core owns reservations, budgets and physical lifetimes; consumers declare extents, representations and reuse plans.
requests: Opt-in bounded keyed requests with request/lane-generation identity; serial fallback is preserved.
request_options: Value-owned sampling options (temperature, top_p, top_k, seed, min_p, penalties, logit_bias, min_tokens), stop-token overrides, logprobs, stop_strings and text, plus immutable shared host extension parameters. Per-field capability and range checks precede admission and name the field; logit_bias ids must be below the valid vocabulary. The runtime passes sampling values through; sessions apply them after reading their logits with crit/sampling.h (resolve_sampling, Sampler, a per-request TokenHistory) or a device path following the same rules, and draws depend only on seed, position and stream. The legacy open_request default refuses any sampling field, context, logprobs, stop_strings or text rather than dropping it. Option payload charges and owners survive through retirement or quarantine.
scoring: Declared scoring on ConcurrentModel uses an exclusive FIFO barrier after all earlier generation retirement. Queued scores share allowance/deadlines; active cancellation drains before discarding. Returned score storage stays owned through settlement or quarantine. Public result capacity is reserved separately from adapter-owned scratch. Declared query scoring returns per target a log-probability, caller-chosen query log-probabilities (finite or negative infinity), an optional argmax and, with top_k (at most max_top_logprobs), ranked alternatives, on a named score path when requested; per_target zero with no ids scores the targets alone. Query ids and targets must be below the valid vocabulary (targets are rejected at submission); results are validated for count, value class, ranking and vocabulary before publication.
progress: Readiness precedes copy/charge of borrowed token rows; model commit precedes publication.
logprobs: Declared token_logprobs returns per generated token its log-probability under the raw logits of the pass that produced it, normalized over the valid vocabulary, and up to max_top_logprobs (at most top_logprobs_limit, 64) ranked alternatives. Core checks counts, value class (never NaN or positive infinity, at most 1e-3 above zero) and distinct valid ids in non-increasing order before commit, trims rows with their tokens and publishes them under the request lock; a violation is a model contract failure. Ids at or above valid_vocabulary never appear as generated tokens, alternatives, argmax or logit_bias entries.
output_events: Handle::wait_output calls its sink once per published token, in order, on the waiting thread and outside the request lock, with the token's log-probability, alternatives and released text; spans and text are valid only during the call. Whatever leaves the sink cancels the request, which is waited for and released before the exit propagates unchanged.
group_failure: Poison/quiesce after failed group commit; publish none of that group and preserve earlier committed output.
retirement: Stop producers and drain backends. Retain/quarantine complete owners when settlement is unproved.
request_release: When wait()/wait_output() returns or rethrows, or a handle is destroyed without a wait, every host charge of a non-quarantined request has been released on that thread. A quarantined runtime retains the request and its charges.
streams: When a backend uses asynchronous queues, submit accesses to explicit services and order cross-queue dependencies. CUDA services are optional.
qualification: Source contracts and host references are separate from native/GPU/model/performance acceptance.
transfer_readiness: Order operation-specific worker/copy completion. An earlier completed event or enqueue success cannot publish new content. Retain source and destination owners through actual settlement.

optional_integrations.scope: Expert caching is a consumer-selected Inference technique; graph capture and shared device allocations with mapped-source resolution are optional Core CUDA services. None is a core integration requirement. Each selected technique owns its representation-specific correctness contract and optional optimization candidates.

tracing: Optional per-engine bounded host event ring, charged to host resources. Nonblocking writers count loss; snapshots do not acquire model locks or synchronize device work. Request/generation and operation identities correlate phases; host durations and step gaps are diagnostics, not GPU timings. Adapter device_timings() add device point events under the enclosing step operation; a throwing hook counts as dropped trace data. Optional operator ranges (crit/trace.h, TraceConfig::operators): a per-engine bounded ring of completed work-annotated host ranges on the same clock, charged to host resources, bound as the operator sink of the threads that run model callbacks and returned in TraceSnapshot::operators; scopes compile out without CRIT_TRACE_ENABLED and add no device fences.
mixed_batches: Optional Profile.max_batch_tokens with ConcurrentModel ModelInfo.mixed_batches enables execute() groups. BatchPolicy.fair rotates minimum grants before expansion; decode_first prioritizes decoders and reserves one unit for the oldest prefill after prefill_starvation_steps waiting groups. Grants sum to the quota. Progress reports actual target/draft/padded work. Membership, readiness, commit, cancellation and retirement invariants apply; per-lane steps remain ordered and kernels are engine supplied.
admission: Up to max_request_concurrency (4096) lanes subject to profile, model declaration and engine memory admission. admission_lookahead defaults to zero (FIFO); positive lookahead permits bounded ready-follower backfill without crossing scoring barriers or max_admission_bypasses for any deferred request. No implicit eviction or recomputation. Linear lane-indexed group identity validation and traces include all rows subject to bounded ring loss. Lane/control metadata is outside payload reservations.
reuse_admission: Optional capability-checked scheduling hints rank a bounded queue window by waited time / estimated remaining nanoseconds. Explicit elapsed-age and bypass limits force FIFO progress. Shared prefix affinity defers duplicate active prefills only until bounded aging; estimates never authorize reuse. Admission/open revalidate state and resources. Score barriers remain exclusive.
prefill_advice: Optional capability-checked latency advice may shrink serial/concurrent prefill grants using occupied context and mixed decode work. Zero preserves the grant; oversized advice fails. Estimates never expand token or memory budgets or guarantee elapsed time.
async_batches: Optional capability-checked max_inflight_batches (1..64) retains prepared BatchExecution owners and stable WorkItems before submit(notify). Adapters publish readiness then notify Core, including failed production; notifications wake the scheduler without replacing the readiness certificate. Independent groups may overlap; a lane has one operation in flight. Nonblocking ready proves physical settlement before progress/commit/publication. Step traces include completion observation and publication; failed spans do not certify settlement. Deadline or cancellation never proves completion. Join producers and notifications in operation quiescence, quiesce model, then drain backend before releasing owners; ambiguous failure quarantines them. Engines budget workspaces, protect shared inspections and transfer new commit-work owners to sessions.
sampling: crit/sampling.h is a library sessions call after reading logits; the runtime never samples. Draws are a pure function of (seed, position, stream, purpose), so trimming, rollback and redo need no generator state, and device code can reproduce them. TokenHistory follows the KV frontier (stage, commit, rollback). Suppress ids outside the sampler row are ignored. Sampler::sample/distribution with AllowedTokens mask every other id before the rules; without it behavior is unchanged.
constraints: Optional structured-output service: crit/constraints.h matchers (finite choices, JSON objects, compiled byte grammars) are request-private, fork/rewind with the model's accepted output and never return an empty allowed set (dead ends and exhausted limits throw; no unconstrained fallback). Vocabularies and grammars are immutable and shared. allowed() walks the vocabulary's piece trie and caches sets by exact matcher state (AllowedCache); the result equals the full-vocabulary scan, chart exhaustion included. crit_core.constraints compiles the documented JSON schema/regex/EBNF subsets into tokenizer-independent artifacts, rejects unsupported constructs, prepares them on bounded workers and derives the tokenizer byte table. The runtime never applies constraints.
state_cache: crit/state.h is bookkeeping only; Core never touches KV or recurrent state bytes. The engine owns storage, writes where a Round points, performs copies through StateStorage hooks and calls the cache from its sessions. begin is failure-atomic and commit consumes the round; ids become allocatable only at reference count zero after retire() of their epoch. Prefix reuse verifies exact tokens and ends where every recurrent component has a snapshot (copied through copy_slot at page boundaries, restored by attach) and every sliding-window group still holds the window's pages; window groups drop pages older than the window.
model_files: crit/json.h, file.h, sha256.h, safetensors.h and model_config.h read model artifacts without decoding tensor values. JSON is strict; non-finite literals load only from config.json and generation_config.json, and typed fields refuse non-finite values and integers beyond 64 bits. Loaders verify that a file did not change while they read it, and check limits before reserving memory. Weight encodings and loading remain engine supplied.
device_services: crit/device_graph.h and crit/device_memory.h are host protocols with no device call: graph identity with settled eviction, staged geometry and a replay state machine where any failure after submission poisons replay; leases charged once through Resources with settled final release, retry only after a failed settle, never after an ambiguous release; mapped extents resolved to one device pointer only across continuous aliases. crit/cuda_graph.h and crit/cuda_memory.h (CRIT_CORE_CUDA) add the CUDA capture harness, lease hooks and host registration; failed drains retain complete owners.
host_memory: crit/host_memory.h observes physical, commit and cgroup headroom (unknown values carry notes) and admits a working set plus reserve against every known domain. Admission is evidence, not a guarantee: charge host reservations through Resources and keep allocation failure authoritative. Device memory is outside it.
